title: Financial Crime Oversight for Boards
summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the understanding and tools to oversee financial crime risk and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips boards and directors to oversee the firm's financial crime risks: setting risk appetite, challenging the MLRO and management, and evidencing effective oversight to supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors a practical understanding of their responsibilities for preventing money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions breaches, fraud, bribery and the facilitation of tax evasion. Participants leave able to set the board's expectations, read financial crime MI critically, oversee remediation and see their firm the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: The board's AML/CFT, sanctions, fraud, bribery and tax evasion responsibilities, financial crime risk appetite, the role and reporting of the MLRO, reading financial crime MI, culture and conduct, supervisory findings and remediation, and directors' personal liability.
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk and audit committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for financial crime, compliance and operations
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
Learning Objectives: Explain the board's responsibilities across AML/CFT, sanctions, fraud, bribery and tax evasion
Set a financial crime risk appetite with measurable limits and escalation triggers
Evaluate the role, independence and reporting of the MLRO
Interpret financial crime MI and identify what is missing
Oversee responses to supervisory findings and remediation programmes
Assess directors' personal exposure and evidence effective oversight
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in financial crime compliance is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)

modules.title: Financial Crime and the Board
modules.summary: Plain-language grounding in the financial crime risks a firm faces, the international standards behind them and why supervisors hold the board accountable for the firm's defences.
objectives: Explain money laundering, terrorist and proliferation financing, sanctions evasion, fraud, bribery and tax evasion
Identify the international standards that shape national requirements
Define the board's responsibilities and distinguish them from management's
syllabus: The financial crime landscape and how criminals exploit financial firms
FATF Recommendations, mutual evaluations and the risk-based approach
Board accountability and senior executive responsibility for financial crime
Lessons from major enforcement cases

modules.title: Risk Assessment and Risk Appetite
modules.summary: How the firm assesses its financial crime exposure across customers, products, channels and geographies, and how the board sets a risk appetite that management can apply.
objectives: Assess the quality of the business-wide financial crime risk assessment
Set a risk appetite with in-scope and prohibited business and measurable limits
Challenge strategic decisions that change the firm's financial crime exposure
syllabus: Business-wide risk assessment: inherent risk, controls and residual risk
Drafting a financial crime risk appetite statement
High-risk customers, jurisdictions, products and new business lines
Growth, de-risking and the board's strategic choices

modules.title: Sanctions, Fraud, Bribery and Tax Evasion
modules.summary: The board's oversight of the financial crime risks beyond money laundering, where liability is often strict and failures can be sudden and severe.
objectives: Explain the board's obligations under sanctions, anti-bribery and tax evasion regimes
Evaluate whether the firm has adequate procedures to prevent these offences
Assess the firm's fraud exposure, including payment scams and internal fraud
syllabus: Sanctions screening, ownership and control, and evasion typologies
Fraud risk: customers, staff, third parties and emerging scams
Bribery and corruption: gifts, intermediaries and adequate procedures
Failure to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion

modules.title: The MLRO and the Financial Crime Function
modules.summary: How the board ensures the MLRO and financial crime function have the standing, independence and resources to do their job, and how it uses their reporting.
objectives: Evaluate the independence, seniority and resourcing of the MLRO
Assess the MLRO's annual report and the board's response to it
Identify warning signs of an under-powered financial crime function
syllabus: Role, access to the board and the MLRO's relationship with the business
Resourcing, systems and the use of outsourced or group functions
The MLRO annual report: what good looks like
Suspicious activity reporting and the national FIU

modules.title: Reading Financial Crime MI
modules.summary: The information boards need to oversee financial crime, how to read MI and dashboards critically, and how to obtain independent assurance rather than relying on assertion.
objectives: Specify the management information and indicators the board needs
Interpret financial crime MI and recognise false comfort
Obtain independent assurance from compliance monitoring and internal audit
syllabus: The core board information set: risk profile, alerts, backlogs and reporting
Key risk indicators: periodic review, screening, transaction monitoring and training
Recognising comfort without evidence and green dashboards
Compliance monitoring, internal audit and external reviews as assurance

modules.title: Culture, Conduct and Speaking Up
modules.summary: How tone from the top, incentives and the board's own behaviour shape whether staff report concerns and whether commercial pressure overrides financial crime controls.
objectives: Assess the firm's financial crime culture and the signals the board sends
Evaluate whether incentives and commercial pressure undermine controls
Identify how the board oversees whistleblowing and speaking up
syllabus: Tone from the top, the middle and the front line
Remuneration, sales incentives and accountability for breaches
Whistleblowing arrangements and the board's champion
Training and awareness that changes behaviour

modules.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation
modules.summary: How the board responds when the authority identifies serious failings, oversees remediation and look-back exercises, and avoids repeat findings.
objectives: Explain how supervisors assess financial crime controls and escalate concerns
Evaluate remediation plans, independent reviews and look-backs
Challenge management on root causes, timelines and sustainable fixes
syllabus: Supervisory inspections, findings letters and risk mitigation programmes
Remediation governance: ownership, milestones and board reporting
Look-backs, independent reviewers and validation of closure
Repeat findings as a sign of a firm that is not learning

modules.title: Personal Liability and the Board's Action Plan
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a board action plan, examining directors' personal exposure and how the board evidences effective financial crime oversight.
objectives: Assess directors' personal regulatory, civil and criminal exposure
Prepare the board to evidence its oversight to supervisors
Produce a board action plan for financial crime oversight
syllabus: Personal accountability, fitness and probity and enforcement against individuals
Reasonable steps: what the minutes and papers need to show
Board skills, training and external advice on financial crime
Workshop: the board's twelve-month financial crime oversight plan
